items.followUp: How does metallic character change down a group and across a period?

rubric.why: Tests the trend across a period.
rubric.description: States that non-metallic character increases from left to right across a period.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct direction and trend.

rubric.why: Tests the trend within a group.
rubric.description: States that non-metallic character decreases down a group (or increases up a group).
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct group trend.

modelAnswer: Across a period, non-metallic character increases from left to right.
Down a group, non-metallic character decreases from top to bottom.

items.followUp: State the difference between an atom and a molecule, giving one example of each.

rubric.why: A compound’s elements are chemically combined in a definite proportion.
rubric.description: States that a compound consists of elements chemically combined in a fixed proportion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for chemical combination and fixed proportion.

rubric.why: A compound has properties different from its constituent elements.
rubric.description: States that a compound’s properties differ from those of its constituent elements.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the property distinction.

rubric.why: Mixture constituents are physically mixed and need not be in a fixed ratio.
rubric.description: States that a mixture has substances physically combined in variable proportions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for physical mixing and variable proportion.

rubric.why: The substances in a mixture retain their individual properties.
rubric.description: States that mixture constituents retain their properties.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the retained-properties distinction.

rubric.why: Mixtures can be separated by physical methods, unlike compounds which require chemical means.
rubric.description: States that mixture components can be separated by physical methods.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct separation method or general statement.

modelAnswer: A compound is a pure substance formed when two or more elements are chemically combined in a fixed proportion by mass.
The properties of a compound are different from the properties of its constituent elements.
A mixture is formed when two or more substances are physically mixed in any proportion.
The substances in a mixture retain their individual properties.
The components of a mixture can be separated by physical methods; the elements of a compound can be separated only by chemical methods.

items.followUp: Write four properties of covalent compounds.

rubric.why: Many ionic compounds form crystalline solids.
rubric.description: Identifies ionic compounds as crystalline solids.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for this property.

rubric.why: Strong electrostatic attractions between ions require considerable energy to overcome.
rubric.description: States that ionic compounds have high melting points or high boiling points.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for either high melting or high boiling point.

rubric.why: Ionic compounds are generally soluble in water.
rubric.description: States that ionic compounds are generally soluble in water.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for this solubility property.

rubric.why: Ions conduct charge when mobile in a melt or aqueous solution.
rubric.description: States that ionic compounds conduct electricity when molten or dissolved in water.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correct electrical conductivity conditions.

modelAnswer: Ionic compounds are usually crystalline solids.
They have high melting and boiling points because of strong electrostatic forces between oppositely charged ions.
They are generally soluble in water.
They conduct electricity in the molten state or in aqueous solution, because their ions are free to move.

items.followUp: Compare the atomic models proposed by Dalton and Thomson.

rubric.why: Rutherford proposed a small, positively charged nucleus.
rubric.description: States that Rutherford’s atom contains a small positive nucleus.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the nucleus and its positive charge.

rubric.why: The scattering experiment showed that most of the atom is empty space.
rubric.description: States that most of the atom is empty space.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for this feature of Rutherford’s model.

rubric.why: Both models describe electrons moving around a central nucleus, but this alone does not distinguish Bohr’s shells.
rubric.description: States that electrons move around the nucleus in Rutherford’s model.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly describing Rutherford’s electrons.

rubric.why: Bohr introduced fixed orbits or energy levels for electrons.
rubric.description: States that Bohr’s electrons occupy fixed energy levels or shells.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the quantised-orbit distinction.

rubric.why: Bohr’s model accounted for atomic stability and energy changes during transitions between levels.
rubric.description: States that Bohr explained stability or that electrons absorb/emit energy when changing energy levels.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct explanation specific to Bohr’s model.

modelAnswer: Rutherford proposed that an atom has a small, positively charged nucleus at its centre, with electrons revolving around it.
Most of the atom is empty space.
Rutherford’s theory did not explain the stability of the atom.
Bohr proposed that electrons revolve around the nucleus only in fixed orbits or energy levels, each having a definite energy.
Electrons do not radiate energy while in a fixed orbit; they absorb or emit energy when they move between energy levels.

items.followUp: Describe diffusion in gases and state two factors that affect its rate.

rubric.why: Diffusion is the spreading and intermixing of particles.
rubric.description: Describes particles intermixing or spreading from a region of higher concentration to lower concentration.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the core description of diffusion.

rubric.why: In liquids, moving particles spread through and intermix with other liquid particles.
rubric.description: Applies diffusion to liquids and explains that their particles move and intermix.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing diffusion in liquids.

rubric.why: Higher temperature gives particles more kinetic energy and increases diffusion rate.
rubric.description: Names temperature and gives its effect on diffusion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the temperature factor and correct effect.

rubric.why: A greater concentration difference or smaller particles can increase diffusion rate.
rubric.description: Names another valid factor, such as concentration difference or particle size, and its effect.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a second factor with a correct effect.

modelAnswer: Diffusion in liquids is the spontaneous intermixing of particles as they move randomly from a region of higher concentration to a region of lower concentration.
Diffusion is slower in liquids than in gases because liquid particles are closer together and experience stronger intermolecular forces.
Temperature affects diffusion: increasing temperature increases particle motion and makes diffusion faster.
Concentration difference affects diffusion: a greater concentration difference makes diffusion faster.

items.followUp: Define a compound and state how many elements are currently known.

rubric.why: An element consists of one kind of atom and cannot be decomposed chemically into simpler substances.
rubric.description: Defines an element as a substance made of one kind of atom that cannot be decomposed chemically.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the definition.

rubric.why: The currently known number of elements is 118.
rubric.description: Gives the number of discovered/known elements as 118.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct number.

modelAnswer: An element is a pure substance made up of only one kind of atom and cannot be broken down into simpler substances by chemical means.
A total of 118 elements have been discovered.

items.followUp: State two properties of a proton.

rubric.why: A neutron has no electrical charge.
rubric.description: States that a neutron is electrically neutral.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the charge property.

rubric.why: A neutron has a mass of approximately one atomic mass unit.
rubric.description: States that a neutron has approximately 1 amu of mass.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the mass property.

modelAnswer: A neutron has no electrical charge; it is neutral.
Its mass is approximately 1 atomic mass unit (amu).

items.followUp: What are the two types of particles found in an atomic nucleus?

rubric.why: Nucleons are the particles found in the nucleus.
rubric.description: Identifies nucleons as particles present in an atom’s nucleus.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying their location.

rubric.why: The term nucleons refers specifically to protons and neutrons.
rubric.description: Names protons and neutrons as nucleons.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for both types of nucleon.

modelAnswer: Nucleons are the particles present in the nucleus of an atom.
They are protons and neutrons.
